brief: An inspiration library for graphic designers: save posters, packaging, type and street photos, find them by colour, turn them into moodboards for clients. Redesign of the whole app and landing page; the current look feels generic and the fonts aren't right.

concepts.label: A
concepts.name: Cutting mat
concepts.idea: The app is the green self-healing cutting mat on a designer's desk, and every saved image is an offcut lying on it.
concepts.why: It comes straight from the name and from the friend's desk. Nobody else's product could use it: a cutting mat is where offcuts are made.

fonts.sample: Poster for Tvornica Kulture, kept for the halftone.

concepts.motion: Only the images move, like paper: saving drops an offcut onto the mat with a little weight, and on the moodboard pieces slide and settle. The interface itself never animates in.
concepts.signature: Saving an image: a scalpel line runs across it and the trimmed offcut drops onto the mat, landing a few degrees off straight.
sections: Landing: one mat, the visitor's tabs fall onto it as offcuts and the count drops to zero; below, three plain sentences and a sign-in
Library: the mat as the page; thumbnails as offcuts with slightly uneven trimmed edges (cut from each image's own hash, so they never change)
Image: lying alone on the mat, its print size at 300 dpi along the mat's ruler, palette as cut colour chips
Moodboard: the mat's grid is the artboard grid; the PDF is the proof

kit.to: The interaction comes from what the product is: here, paper on a mat
Images laid on a table at slightly different sizes, not a perfect grid
One bold colour carries the whole brand: mat green instead of safety orange
The saved images are the spectacle; the mat around them stays plain
Its drag-and-drop becomes the moodboard on the mat, with paper weight instead of a doll
No WebGL, no cursor, no grain: the mat is flat colour and a printed grid

new: Trimmed-edge thumbnails (clip-path from the image hash)
Mat ruler showing real print sizes
risks: A measuring grid is design-tool chrome in the tell list; it's allowed only because a cutting mat really has one, so it stays on the mat surfaces, faint
Green everywhere could tire in daily use; needs a light mat variant (the grey side of a mat) for long sessions
Uneven edges must stay subtle or the library looks messy

images.caption: lib-muller: one flat colour carries the whole brand (principle)
lib-rm-wrillustrations: work laid on a table, slightly different sizes (principle)
lib-an: the interaction is the product (principle)

concepts.label: B
concepts.name: Fan deck
concepts.idea: The library is filed like a Pantone fan deck: by colour first, and the only colour in the interface is the colour of what you saved.
concepts.why: Offcut's real difference is that it knows every image's colours. Designers already think in fan decks and swatch books, so the colour index becomes the navigation.
concepts.motion: One thing moves: the fan. Choosing a colour fans the chips open around a pivot and the wall of thumbnails re-sorts (Flip), the ones without that colour dropping to a faint grey. Nothing else animates.
concepts.signature: The fan deck at the top of the library is made from the colours actually in your library, ordered by hue. Fan it open, touch a chip, and your whole library re-files itself by that colour.
sections: Landing: a fan deck made from twelve drawn posters opens across the page; touching a chip sorts the posters below it
Library: a dense wall of small thumbnails hanging from one top line (ragged bottom), the fan above; all type one size
Image: the image, and its palette as tall fan-deck chips with HEX, RGB and CMYK printed on each
Boards and moodboard: white, no frames; feedback as plain counts

kit.to: The whole library as a wall of small thumbnails; colour instead of DIA's greyscale
Non-matching images drop to a faint grey; one set of thumbnails, re-sorted with Flip
One small size for all type; hierarchy only from black and grey
Thumbnails hang from one top line with a ragged bottom edge
Its pure black on white and small type; serif dropped, one grotesk only
No scroll scenes, no WebGL: the fan is the only motion

new: Fan-deck colour index generated from the library's own palettes
Hue ordering and chip fan animation
risks: Very quiet: if the fan isn't great, the app reads as plain
Small type everywhere needs care for accessibility (13px minimum, real contrast)
An empty library has no colours to fan: needs a first-run state

images.caption: lib-rm-dia: the archive as a wall of thumbnails (reworked: in colour)
lib-obys-grid: faint tiles, one set of thumbnails in several layouts
lib-and2es-pills: one tiny size, hierarchy from fill
lib-rm-oppen: hang everything from one line

concepts.label: C
concepts.name: Poster column
concepts.idea: Offcut is a Zagreb advertising column: a round green pillar where every poster you saved is pasted over the last.
concepts.why: It's from your friend's city and from what graphic designers love most in it: street posters, layered and torn. The column turns, so your library is something you walk around.

fonts.sample: Kept from Ilica, a gig poster half covered by the next one.

concepts.motion: The column turns slowly; drag pushes it, hover slows it down. In the app, presentation mode opens by turning the column to the image. Everything else is still.
concepts.signature: The landing page and every board's presentation open on a column of that board's images, pasted edge to edge in overlapping layers, turning in the middle of the screen.
sections: Landing: the column, with drawn posters pasted on it; a condensed headline on a pasted strip; plain text below
Library: images pasted edge to edge with no gaps, like a hoarding; captions in the serif
Boards: each board has its own small column as its cover
Presentation: the column turns to each image, then it fills the screen

kit.to: Images around a turning 3D object; rings become a cylinder of pasted posters
Hover slows the whole column so a poster can be read
The caption slides up at the bottom centre: title in the serif, designer beside it
Tall posters are the loud thing; everything else whispers
Its spiral and cone shapes become a cylinder with overlapping, slightly rotated layers

new: Cylinder shape with layered pasting for orbit-gallery
risks: A 3D signature risks the 'every site is a toy' tell, so it stays on the landing page and the presentation intro only
Condensed caps headline is close to the kit's default hero; it has to be on a pasted strip, never floating
